Nothing in episodes/event_steps/topic_facts/semantic_triples/object_states names a 'phase 2' start time or gives a dodge count, so the count is a pure frame-by-frame visual task with no text scaffold, and even the phase-2 boundary itself has to be inferred visually -- rollouts disagreed on it by up to ~120s (73920s vs 74257s).

root_causes: The memory DB's auto-generated captions for this fight are internally inconsistent (the same continuous boss fight is described as several different-looking monsters across 30s buckets) and never state a phase-2 boundary, so every rollout had to guess where phase 2 starts purely from clip_qa, and the five guesses ranged from ~73920s to ~74257s -- a >100s disagreement on the counting window itself.

clip_qa's frame-sampling density appears to scale down as the requested window widens: calls over long windows (150-210s) systematically under-detect brief dodge/parry flash events in the later part of the window (rollout-1 explicitly reported 'no additional event' in a span where a separately-windowed call in rollout-0 did find one), while calls over short windows (30s) over-detect, with one 30s sub-window alone matching the entire reference count of 8 (rollout-3).

When phase 2 was split across multiple clip_qa calls (rollouts 0, 2, 3, 4), each sub-agent call was answered independently with no shared frame-level bookkeeping, so counts were summed with no de-duplication of events straddling a window boundary and no sanity check against the other windows' totals.

No rollout cross-checked the final total against any other source (e.g. requesting a second independent full-phase-2 clip_qa pass, or checking event_steps/object_states for corroborating counter-hit records) before submitting, so an implausible total (1 or 18) was submitted with the same confidence as a plausible one (7).
what_worked: All five rollouts correctly localized the general boss-fight window (73991-74267) via semantic_search/run_sql and correctly identified the boss as 碧水金睛兽 / 妖王·翠云金睛兽, so retrieval of the right episode was not the failure mode.

Multiple rollouts (0, 1, 4) independently converged on a real dodge cluster around ~74136-74166s, suggesting clip_qa can detect genuine perfect-dodge visual effects when the window is narrow enough, even though none of them found the complete set of 8.
transferable_lessons: For fine-grained visual counting questions, first pin down the exact sub-interval (here, the phase-2 boundary) with a dedicated clip_qa call before counting, and re-verify that boundary with a second independent call if the fight window is long and boss forms visually vary -- do not let the counting call and the phase-boundary call be conflated in one arbitrary window split.

Keep clip_qa windows short and of consistent, deliberately overlapping length (e.g. 20-30s with a few seconds of overlap) when counting rapid discrete events across a longer interval, and explicitly reconcile events that fall near a window boundary to avoid double counting or dropped events between calls.

When independent clip_qa calls covering adjacent/overlapping windows disagree (e.g. one says an interval has no more events, another finds one there), that disagreement is itself signal that the counting task needs a re-check, not something to silently resolve by picking one call's number.

Before submitting a count, sanity-check it against the coarse DB evidence available (e.g. total fight duration, defeat timestamp) and flag implausible outputs like a single 30s sub-window already matching or exceeding the full reference-scale total, or a phase reduced to under 15 seconds.
